So the packed values land at arbitrary offsets up to nlocal*size_history (outside both the transmitted window and, in general, the allocated buffer). Both sibling implementations index by the send slot: fix_neigh_history_kokkos.cpp:383-385 'int m = nsend + offset; d_buf(mysend) = d_ubuf(m).d;' and fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:186-187 'int m = nsend + offset; d_buf[mysend] = m;'. Nothing compensates elsewhere -- the unpack side (line 422) also assumes slot-major layout ('int m = i*size_history'), which is only consistent with a slot-indexed pack.

reasoning: The pairstyle half is real. FixWallGranKokkos derives from FixWallGranOld (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.h:38), whose constructor accepts 'granular' (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:83 'else if (strcmp(arg[3],"granular") == 0) pairstyle = GRANULAR;') and whose class enum is 'HOOKE, HOOKE_HISTORY, HERTZ_HISTORY, GRANULAR' (fix_wall_gran_old.h:29). post_force (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:107-119) is 'if (pairstyle == HOOKE) error->all(...); else if (pairstyle == HOOKE_HISTORY) {...} else if (pairstyle == HERTZ_HISTORY) error->all(...);' with no trailing else, so pairstyle == GRANULAR launches no kernel and raises no error; the fix silently applies zero wall force. Since the style is registered as wall/gran/kk (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.h:16), 'fix ... wall/gran granular ...' under -sf kk hits exactly this path. Note the class-scope enumerators win over the file-local 'enum{HOOKE,HOOKE_HISTORY,HERTZ_HISTORY,BONDED_HISTORY};' at line 24 (member lookup precedes namespace lookup) and both have the same numeric values, so the shadowing enum is only a readability problem, not the cause. fix: Add a final 'else error->all(FLERR, "Fix wall/gran/kk does not yet support the granular interaction style");' to the pairstyle chain in FixWallGranKokkos::post_force, and an 'else error->all(FLERR, ...)' (or a check in init()) for wallstyle values other than XPLANE/YPLANE/ZPLANE/ZCYLINDER. Better still, reject the unsupported pairstyle/wallstyle in FixWallGranKokkos::init() so the error appears at setup rather than on every timestep. Also rename the file-local enumerator BONDED_HISTORY to GRANULAR (or delete the shadowing enum) so it matches fix_wall_gran_old.h.

reasoning: Traced the whole allocation path. FixWallGranOld's constructor calls the qualified 'FixWallGranOld::grow_arrays(atom->nmax)' (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:450) which allocates BOTH history_one and, when peratom_flag, array_atom (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:1567-1573). The Kokkos constructor then destroys history_one and calls the virtual grow_arrays again (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:44); every later growth goes through Atom::grow -> fix->grow_arrays(nmax) i.e. the Kokkos override (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:303-311), which grows only k_history_one and only 'if (use_history)'. array_atom therefore stays frozen at the initial atom->nmax. The base pack_exchange/copy_arrays that the Kokkos class delegates to still touch it: fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:1584-1587 'array_atom[j][m] = array_atom[i][m];' and :1616-1619 'buf[n++] = array_atom[i][m];'. 'contacts' is a real keyword accepted by the shared constructor (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:410-413, peratom_flag=1, size_peratom_cols=8), so this is reachable with wall/gran/kk. Separately the constructor sets 'maxexchange = size_history;' (line 35) while FixWallGranOld::pack_exchange writes size_history+size_peratom_cols doubles, which undersizes both Comm::maxexchange_fix on the host path and the 'nsend*fix_iextra->maxexchange' grow in comm_kokkos.cpp:1371. And the device kernel never writes array_atom nor calls clear_stored_contacts(), which the CPU post_force does (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:637-639, 713-724), so the per-atom contact output is always zero.
fix: Simplest correct fix: reject the 'contacts' keyword (peratom_flag) in FixWallGranKokkos::init() with an explicit error, as is already done for fix_rigid. If it is to be supported: call FixWallGranOld::grow_arrays()/copy_arrays()/set_arrays() unconditionally for the array_atom part from the Kokkos overrides (they must run even when use_history is 0), set 'maxexchange = size_history + (peratom_flag ? size_peratom_cols : 0);' in the constructor, and have the kernel fill array_atom (plus a clear_stored_contacts equivalent).

reasoning: All three claimed omissions are real, and there is a fourth, worse one. (1) pack_exchange_kokkos (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:386-411) syncs 'k_history_one.template sync<DeviceType>()' and then runs a kernel that writes d_history_one for the copylist compaction (:377-379), but never calls modify<DeviceType>(); fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:239 and fix_neigh_history_kokkos.cpp:443-445 both do. It also never calls 'k_buf.modify<DeviceType>()' + sync to the requested space, which fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:235-238 does. (2) unpack_exchange_kokkos (:431-450) writes the device view and calls modify<DeviceType>() at :449 with no preceding sync<DeviceType>() -- compare fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:285. It also omits 'k_buf.sync<DeviceType>()'/'k_indices.sync<DeviceType>()' (fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:274-275). (3) unpack_exchange (:353-361) calls the base (which writes history_one on the host) and then modify_host() without a sync_host(); its own pack_exchange at :346 and fix_neigh_history_kokkos.cpp:515-517 do sync first. (4) NOT IN THE FINDING but more consequential: post_force (:70-124) writes d_history_one in the kernel every timestep and never calls k_history_one.modify<DeviceType>() either -- nothing in the file marks the shear history device-modified except unpack_exchange_kokkos:449. So on a GPU build the DualView believes host and device are in sync while the host copy is stale from the first timestep on, and any host-side path that then calls modify_host (copy_arrays during delete_atoms, unpack_exchange) makes that stale copy authoritative and the accumulated shear history is silently discarded.
fix: Add 'k_history_one.template modify<DeviceType>();' at the end of post_force (after the parallel_for) and at the end of pack_exchange_kokkos; add 'k_history_one.template sync<DeviceType>();' before the parallel_for in unpack_exchange_kokkos, together with 'k_buf.sync<DeviceType>(); k_indices.sync<DeviceType>();'; add 'k_buf.modify<DeviceType>();' plus the 'if (space == Host) k_buf.sync_host(); else k_buf.sync_device();' pair at the end of pack_exchange_kokkos; and add 'k_history_one.sync_host();' at the start of unpack_exchange.
